import pandas as pd

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

# Display the first few rows and the data types
df_info = df.info()
df_head = df.head()

df_info, df_head

# Drop rows with missing values in 'body_mass_index' and 'blood_pressure'
df_cleaned = df.dropna(subset=['body_mass_index', 'blood_pressure'])

# Check the shape of the cleaned dataset
cleaned_shape = df_cleaned.shape
cleaned_shape

from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Initialize the Kaplan-Meier fitter
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()

# Fit the model
kmf.fit(durations=df_cleaned['follow_up_time'], event_observed=df_cleaned['event_observed'])

# Plot the survival curve
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
kmf.plot_survival_function()
plt.title('Kaplan-Meier Survival Curve')
plt.xlabel('Follow-up Time')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
plt.grid()
plt.show()

# Calculate the median survival time
median_survival_time = kmf.median_survival_time_
median_survival_time

from lifelines import CoxPHFitter

# Prepare the data for the Cox model
cox_data = df_cleaned[['follow_up_time', 'event_observed', 'gender', 'body_mass_index', 'blood_pressure', 'cholesterol_level']]

# Fit the Cox Proportional Hazards model
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(cox_data, duration_col='follow_up_time', event_col='event_observed')

# Get the summary of the Cox model
cox_summary = cph.summary

# Extract the p-value and hazard ratio for 'body_mass_index'
hazard_ratio_bmi = cox_summary.loc['body_mass_index', 'exp(coef)']
p_value_bmi = cox_summary.loc['body_mass_index', 'p']

hazard_ratio_bmi, p_value_bmi
